change: String at:, byteAt: and copyFrom:to: read only the requested bytes instead of cloning the entire source; their already-bounded numeric indices use a local array.

contract.before: Perform current index conversions, validate and clone the complete owned String, select the byte/range, then invoke current result constructors.
contract.after: Perform the same conversions and representation/bounds checks, snapshot only the selected byte/range under the String owner's private borrow, release that borrow, then invoke the same result constructors.
preserved: String.fromBytes: remains replaceable; the change does not call the private allocator instead.
Integer/Float dependency context messages and numeric conversions retain their order.
Binary data, negative/out-of-range results and wrong-representation error precedence are unchanged.
No private buffer borrow spans a callback or collection.
Other string searches and numeric parsing retain their previous byte snapshots.

benchmark.scope: Existing String operations through Id on 64-byte, 4-KiB and 1-MiB inputs. Read one byte/character or an eight-byte slice. Five samples/process; serial ABBA. Automatic GC disabled for timed work; explicit precise GC outside every sample. Results checked.

validation: Full Oop core/compiler/GC suite and negative dispatch/construction contracts.

Expanded String/Error ownership test: binary indexing/slicing, empty ranges, bounds, wrong receiver representation, live result-constructor replacement, and collection during both index conversion and result construction.
limits: Local CPU microbenchmarks; the large gains apply to small indexed results from large input strings. They are not whole-application speedups.
Automatic GC disabled only for timed benchmark work; explicit collection occurs outside samples. Runtime policy is unchanged.
This removes native temporary copies and an index vector; required managed result construction remains.
No installed user prefix was replaced. The temporary benchmark caller was removed, and its source is embedded here.
